ruling.recommended_action: Issue a voucher of $3.00 to the rider (RD-2, NS-7) and send the driver's account to Ryde account review for a repeated upheld route deviation + flag_account.
ruling.reasoning:
RydeTAXI is a metered service, so the fare moves with distance and an unexplained deviation is refundable in kilometres [F1][F4][RD-1][RD-2]. The trip is a single off-route segment: 12:12–12:16, 2.93 km driven where the optimal route covers 0.80 km, adding 2.13 km and straying up to 954 m from the optimal route [F3].

No exemption applies. The driver's post-trip statement "I went where the GPS sent me; it rerouted" is a claim, and no rider message agrees to anything before 12:12 — there is no in-app chat at all [F7][F8][RD-5]. RD-3 fails for the same reason: there is no rider message naming a place before the segment [F7][F8][RD-3]. The traffic records do not rescue the segment either: Ayer Rajah Expressway band 4 (30–39 km/h) and Jurong Town Hall Road band 5 (40–49 km/h) are not band 1 or 2, and no incident was recorded near the route in the trip window, so there is no reasonable cause under RD-4 [F9][F10][F11][RD-4]. Fair weather and no rain remove any other excuse [F12].

The refund follows the trace formula: the segment's extra_km (2.13) × this trip's per-km rate ($15.14 ÷ 10.74 km = $1.4097/km) = $3.0027, i.e. $3.00 to the nearest cent [F3][F6][F4][RD-2]. The rider's "app estimated 8 km, meter ended at 11 km" framing asks for the whole ~2.3 km gap, but RD-2 refunds only the measured non-exempt segment's extra_km [F1][F3][RD-2]. Distance outside the segment (corridor returns, map-matching jitter) and the metered waiting time are not refundable [F6][RD-2][RD-3].

RD-6 is satisfied on top of the refund: the driver's profile shows 2 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days (and 4 disputes total), so this case makes the breach repeated and an account flag is required [F14][RD-6]. The rider's profile (1 dispute, 0 upheld) does not decide anything by itself and adds no action here [F13][RD-6].

Safety: I read the complaint, the driver's statement and the (empty) chat — no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation appears, so the screen is clean [F7][F8]. The record is complete enough to decide the segment (GPS trace, fare breakdown, traffic and weather all present), so no evidence gap affects this ruling [F3][F6][F9][F11][RD-2].
